title: 2026年股市將崩盤？「這張圖」超神準預言...小童：網路泡沫、金融海嘯、2020年疫情大跌全抓到 | 聯合新聞網
content: An analyst on UDN discusses a century‑old cycle diagram (Bennett cycle) that supposedly predicts market highs and lows. The diagram shows 11‑year cycles for corn and pork, 11‑year highs for cotton, and a 27‑year cycle for iron with highs every 8‑10 years and lows every 7‑9‑11 years. The author claims the diagram, updated to 2059, marked ABC points where 'A表示空頭的開始', 'B表示是高價賣出的時機', and 'C表示跌深後的多頭反轉'. He cites that the diagram captured major downturns of the past decade, including the 2020 pandemic crash and the 2023 sell‑off, and that the next predicted sell point falls in 2026. The piece also references a “red‑green‑light” indicator that, according to him, has not yet turned red since April, implying the current bullish trend continues. The author warns that if the red‑green indicator turns red or the cycle shows a bearish reversal, investors should be cautious. He frames these observations as evidence that the market is near a high and may reverse soon.

title: Closing Grain and Livestock Futures: August 26, 2025
content: The grain and livestock futures market closed on August 26, 2025 with the following key price movements: 'Sep. corn closed at $3.87 and 1/2, down 1 and 3/4 cents'; 'Sep. soybeans closed at $10.28 and 3/4, up 3 and 1/4 cents'; 'Sep. soybean meal closed at $297.20, up $1.50'; 'Sep. soybean oil closed at 52.76, down 155 points'; and 'Sep. wheat closed at $5.09 and 1/2, up 2 and 3/4 cents'. title: Is the Stock Market Open for Columbus Day? Here's the Fall and Winter Holiday Schedule
content: The U.S. stock markets will remain open on Monday, October 13, 2025, for Columbus Day, while the U.S. bond markets will close in observance of the holiday, which is also recognized as Indigenous Peoples Day in some regions. Bond markets will close again on Tuesday, November 11, for Veterans Day. Stock and bond markets will both close on Thursday, November 27, for Thanksgiving; bond markets will close at 2 p.m. on the following day, while stock markets will close at 1 p.m. Both markets will close on Thursday, December 25, for Christmas; bond markets will close at 2 p.m. on December 24, and stock markets will close at 1 p.m. on December 25. Additionally, both markets will close on Thursday, January 1, 2026, for New Year's Day, with bond markets closing at 2 p.m. on January 1, 2026, and stock markets closing at 1 p.m. on the same day. According to Yahoo! Finance, the holiday trading schedule for fall and winter 2025–2026 has been published.

title: Stock market holiday: Is US stock market closed or open today for Labor Day 2025? | Stock Market News

title: Stock market holidays: BSE, NSE to remain closed on THESE days in October 2025; check full list here | Stock Market News
content: According to the official trading holiday calendar released by the NSE and BSE, the Indian stock market will be closed on three occasions in October 2025, with a special Diwali Muhurat trading session scheduled for 1:45 pm–2:45 pm. The BSE and NSE will remain shut for 11 days in October, including Saturdays and Sundays, while the MCX and currency derivatives will also be closed for three days. The NSE circular states, 'All trades executed in this Diwali Muhurat trading session shall result in settlement obligations,' and notes that the session, normally held in the evening, will take place in the afternoon. Trading will cover equity, commodity derivatives, currency derivatives, equity futures & options, and securities lending & borrowing within the same window. Historically, Muhurat sessions have produced positive returns; in the last 16 years the benchmark indices have closed in the green on 13 occasions. In 2024 the Sensex and Nifty 50 finished the Muhurat session on a strong note, with the BSE Sensex rising 335 points (0.42%) to 79,724 and the Nifty 50 advancing 99 points (0.41%) to 24,304.

title: Borse ai massimi: si avvicina il momento buono per vendere?
content: The stock market is experiencing strong performances worldwide, reaching new historical highs in the US (S&P500). However, despite the current momentum, there are signs of weakness beneath the surface. No market growth phase is infinite, and this one is no exception. While there is no current pessimism, things could change by next autumn, a time when it would be wise to be liquid or even short on stock market indices. Several factors suggest this scenario may unfold, with the analysis focusing on the US market, but with global repercussions if the US market were to decline. As one analyst notes, 'it's possible that the current upward trend could continue for a while, but it's also a good time to consider selling in a strong market, as no growth phase is infinite.'
